subject: NatWest Group plc
title: Growth and productivity need acquisition-adjusted attribution
economic_mechanism: Published CAL stocks increased by£110.9bn, while the stated£42.3bn growth measure uses an Evelyn FY2025-inclusive comparator. Neither is an organic deposit-flow measure. Central-item deposit treatment separately changes the defined stock.
existing_response: Evelyn integration, reported gross cost savings and positive Group profit are existing responses and counterevidence to a generic missing-transformation thesis.
counter: Gross savings are not net financial benefit; no failure, unmet external scope or incremental budget is established.
falsifier: A source-matched organic/acquired bridge and net-benefit reconciliation could show the remaining attribution issue is already resolved.
role: Group finance/integration roles; no purchasing authority or named buyer inferred
possible_open_decision: Measurement and remaining integration choices may remain; no unallocated supplier decision is proven.

subject: HSBC UK Bank plc
title: UK-bank earnings require a USD legal-entity bridge
economic_mechanism: USD 11054m revenue minus701m ECL and4270m costs plus1m associates reconciles to 6084m PBT. These are UK legal-bank9M results, not Group-quarter earnings or GBP.
existing_response: A positive-profit UK franchise and existing legal-entity reporting are evidenced. Global organisational simplification cannot be asserted as a specific UK-bank remedy without applicability evidence.
counter: Aggregate ECL and expense levels do not establish a process/control defect, external delivery requirement or open procurement.
falsifier: UK-specific segment, operating-model and benefit disclosures may explain the movements without any residual commercial problem.
role: UK bank finance/credit/operations roles; Group CEO is not assumed to be UK-bank decision owner
possible_open_decision: UK-specific operating or investment choices remain unproven; only an evidence demand is justified.

subject: Santander UK Group Holdings plc
title: TSB earnings contribution and integration phases are different decisions
economic_mechanism: Group income less separately stated expense, impairment and restructuring/provisions reconciles to£1158m PBT. TSB contribution£96m and costs£327m cover May–September, not nine months or standalone TSB accounts.
existing_response: Acquisition, consolidation and central employer transfer are already completed as reported; proposed legal transfer remains conditional and subsequent systems/customer-data migration is distinct.
counter: Decided acquisition/integration is not an early strategic sales opening. Provisions and integration costs are not supplier funding or currently unallocated scope.
falsifier: Detailed disclosed migration/design responsibilities and contracts may show all material choices already allocated internally or to incumbents.
role: Group finance/integration and legal-entity operations roles; no buying authority inferred
possible_open_decision: Some detailed migration decisions may remain, but no external scope, open procurement or opportunity to shape is established.
